etymology: English: the signature withdrawn by the hand that wrote it - exit announced as sovereignty.
effect: The capability of a signatory to leave an agreement it wrote: the obligations are kept as options, and withdrawal is presented as a return to first principles.
available_to: Any state whose word is worth more abroad than its exit is worth at home.
counter: Make the exit cost something durable: a successor agreement that names the withdrawal penalty, and allies who price the exit into everything that follows.
senses: The capability of a government to treat its own treaty as a policy preference: the accord is binding until it is inconvenient, and the withdrawal is announced in the language of liberation.

It works because the benefit of a treaty is paid over decades and the cost of leaving is paid once, in a news cycle. A signatory that keeps the benefits and drops the obligations has arbitraged its own credibility, and the bill arrives as a premium on every later promise.
example: *"We are withdrawing from the agreement to protect our sovereignty" - the treaty had been drafted by the same government, and **breaking treaties** was the sovereignty in question.*

confused_with.tell: Signaway gives away a right in the fine print; breaking treaties takes back a promise in the headline.
